requirements.statement: In each data table, each th element whose content applies to the whole row or the whole column and that has a scope attribute has scope="row" if it is a row header, or scope="col" if it is a column header.

citations.quote: Pour chaque contenu de balise `<th>` s’appliquant à la totalité de la ligne ou de la colonne et possédant un attribut `scope`, la balise `<th>` vérifie-t-elle une de ces conditions ?

routes.statement: The th is a row header and its scope attribute has the value row.

citations.quote: La balise `<th>` possède un attribut `scope` avec la valeur `"row"` pour les en-têtes de ligne ;
Soit une valeur `"row"` pour les en-têtes de ligne ;

routes.statement: The th is a column header and its scope attribute has the value col.

citations.quote: La balise `<th>` possède un attribut `scope` avec la valeur `"col"` pour les en-têtes de colonne.
Soit une valeur `"col"` pour les en-têtes de colonne.

rationale.text: One requirement with two routes, each tied to a kind of header: scope="row" for a row header, scope="col" for a column header. The value is an attribute that code can read; which kind of header a th is, and whether it applies to the whole row or column, are not. A header is a cell whose content serves as the label of all or part of its row or column, so a th with scope="col" fails only if it is in fact a row header, and its position alone does not prove that. Even a th whose scope value is neither row nor col, such as a misspelt value, fails this test only if it applies to the whole row or column; if it covers a part, the test does not apply to it and test 5.7.3 does. The wording does not say whether a th with scope="rowgroup" or scope="colgroup" applies to the whole row or column. And whether a table element is a data table rather than a layout table is judgment (see 5.1.1). So no th is surely in scope with a sure fault, and the entry is none. No axe rule is tagged for this test, so there are no links. Applicability is judgment. Needs is empty: th elements are cells of table elements, read on the page as loaded.

citations.entry: En-tête de colonne ou de ligne
citations.quote: qui sert d’intitulé pour la totalité ou une partie des cellules de la colonne ou de la ligne.
La balise `<th>` ne possède pas d’attribut `scope` ;
Si c’est le cas pour chaque en-tête s’appliquant à la totalité de la ligne ou de la colonne et pourvu d’un attribut `scope`, **le test est validé**.
